design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (loan_funding_fee_and_entitlement) — self-contained dossier (revision 2, after the policy-task audit).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 5]}. Root loan_ext_substitution_restoration (5 factors); prerequisites loan_ext_assumption_guaranty_in_force (4) and loan_ext_default_partial_claim (4). Chain root -> release -> partial claim; both edges value_input.

[Why a good test] The seller asks only for his entitlement back now that a veteran buyer is assuming his Chesapeake loan with her own entitlement. The substitution rule: "A seller's entitlement is not restored by substitution until the loan record shows the seller released from liability on the assumption." The record shows the loan in_default, release false; only the release write produces the release, and the release is the veteran's own request as seller (blueprint), so the agent hands it over. The release rule: "The guaranty that stays in force on an assumed loan is fixed only after the loan record shows the loan current again, with every reported default cured by a partial claim entry in its money transactions." The loan is in default; only the partial claim write cures a default. Three figures on three successive worlds.

[Scope] Task 0 owns the refund and the liquidated-loan restoration. Task 1 owns loan_ext_default_partial_claim (record_partial_claim_d52e4f0e, agent), loan_ext_assumption_guaranty_in_force (request_release_of_liability_741ed869, user), loan_ext_substitution_restoration (restore_entitlement_by_substitution_1ad1d2fb, agent). Disjoint, jointly all five.

[Problem-tree card] Edge A substitution -> release: value_input, gate substitution_base, form state, negated direction ("not ... until"); opening: status in_default, release_of_liability false; deletion: 69852.13 instead of 32168.77. Edge B release -> partial claim: value_input, gate balance_basis, form state, affirmative ("only after"); opening: status in_default, latest partial claim 2024-02-12 cured an earlier default; deletion: guaranty 63283.28 instead of 42316.64 and restoration 41749.24 instead of 32168.77. Each state is produced by exactly one write of the difficulty. Order: partial claim (8) -> release (10, user) -> substitution (12). The persona never names a partial claim, a release or a step to do first; tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card] Partial claim: loan_evt_default_servicing.partial_claim_delinquency (in_default at handling time: satisfied). Release: loan_evt_assumption (policy scope; requested by the seller). Substitution: loan_evt_entitlement_restoration.loan_closed_for_restoration (released_by_assumption after step 10), loan_agg_entitlement scope. Declared overwrites: partial claim ceiling clause; restoration clause "or when a qualifying veteran buyer assumes the loan and substitutes their own entitlement." (narrowed so the ordinary paid-in-full restoration trigger stays in force, audit O-9); loan_evt_assumption "The veteran's entitlement stays charged after a release unless the buyer is a veteran who substitutes entitlement." (audit F-4) -> "When the buyer substitutes, the part of the seller's entitlement that this restoration does not restore stays charged to the loan."

[Business-object card] Chesapeake loan 796b9feb... (512208846130), not the Virginia Beach rental 88615493... (active, 81800.00 entitlement charged, seeded as a charge row). Ledger: partial claim 9480.00 (2024-02-12), repayments 1200.00 (2025-03-14) and 1200.00 (2025-09-10), entitlement 80000.00. The loan record's partial_claim_balance 7080.00 equals the ledger's principal (9480.00 - 2400.00); the partial claim policy's tier value is the principal plus accrued interest (7221.60), so the field does not stand in for the tier. Comp award 30% running; compensation overpayment 1236.40 active. Buyer named by the caller: Annalise K. Brandt.

[Factor cards]
Partial claim 82799.71 (baseline 90073.87): repeat_claim_ceiling 25% (31 months; baseline 30% -> 99392.02); partial_claim_still_owed (method) — latest claim at least twelve months old -> principal still owed plus 1% simple interest per whole year: (9480.00 - 2400.00) x 1.02 = 7221.60 (other tiers: latest within the year with repayments -> paid less repaid; otherwise -> paid; baseline 9480.00 -> 80541.31); service_connected_ceiling_uplift +2.5 (baseline 0 -> 74503.55); other_debt_reduction 1236.40 (baseline 0 -> 84036.11).
Guaranty in force 42316.64 (baseline 80000.00, the guaranty on the record): guaranty_balance_basis UPB less the partial claim owed 331846.22 - 89879.71 = 241966.51 (baseline loan amount -> 61560.00); cure_carry_share 90 (paid today; baseline 100 -> 47018.49); early_assumption_carry 95 (52 months; baseline 100 -> 44543.83); repeat_claim_carry 90 (two claims; baseline 100 -> 47018.49). Rate = recorded guaranty / loan amount.
Substitution 32168.77 (baseline 80000.00): substitution_measure (method) — guaranty in force below the entitlement still charged and not below the 36000.00 basic entitlement -> the guaranty in force 42316.64; guaranty in force below both -> the basic entitlement (never more than the entitlement still charged); otherwise the entitlement still charged (baseline -> 69852.13); partial_claim_reserve 15% (owed 89879.71 exceeds the guaranty in force; baseline 0 -> 42280.24); reserve_service_connected_relief 25% (30% rating; baseline 0 -> 28798.28); overpayment_reserve 1236.40 (baseline 0 -> 33405.17); repayment_credit 50% of 2400.00 (baseline 0 -> 30968.77). Result capped at the entitlement still charged.
Near-misses: the 2024 partial claim is outside the 24-month recent window; the rental loan's 81800.00 charge is not charged to the Chesapeake loan; owed 89879.71 exceeds the guaranty in force, so the above-guaranty reserve applies.

[Revision 2 — audit items] F-2: the band-rate factor was removed; the rate is the recorded guaranty over the loan amount. F-4: overwrite declared. F-7: every "loan current"/"in default" tier and conjunct was removed from the guaranty ladders; the four factors now turn on the partial claim owed, the age of the latest partial claim, time since closing and the count of partial claims. F-8: every "released by assumption"/"active or in default"/"paid in full" tier and conjunct was removed from the substitution ladders; the measure turns on whether a restoration was already booked and on the guaranty in force, the reserve on whether the partial claim owed exceeds the guaranty in force, plus a new comp-rating relief on that reserve. Stamp: the partial claim still owed no longer reads partial_claim_balance, which is now a declared stale value. Edge B load-bearing text recomputed consistently. Seed: the rental loan's entitlement charge row added (and read).

[Revision 3 — audit items] R2-F8: the substitution measure's tier "a restoration has already been booked" (empty under the base rule that each loan's entitlement is restored only once) and its universal conjunct were removed; the second tier is now a rate reduction refinance on which no entitlement was charged (it carries the entitlement of the loan it replaced), which restores the guaranty in force capped at the basic entitlement — a live, distinct outcome; tier 1 now requires entitlement charged on the loan. N-3: the loan record's partial_claim_balance is reseeded at 7080.00, consistent with the ledger and the account definition; to keep the field from standing in for the still-owed tier, that tier now adds the partial claim's 1% simple interest per whole year once the latest claim is a year old (7221.60), and the quantity is named the partial claim debt carried against the ceiling. Figures recomputed: 82799.71 / 42316.64 / 32168.77.

[Revision 4 — audit item R3-F8] The IRRRL tier of the substitution measure could never move the scored value (on such a loan the entitlement still charged is 0 and the result is capped at it). It is replaced by a tier on the basic entitlement: where the guaranty in force is below both the entitlement still charged and the 36000.00 basic entitlement, the measure is the basic entitlement (never more than the entitlement still charged); tier 1 is now the guaranty in force where it is below the entitlement still charged but not below the basic entitlement. The three tiers are disjoint and each gives its own value on its own domain (e.g. guaranty in force 30000.00 on this loan: tier 2 gives 36000.00, the fall-through 80000.00, tier 1's formula 30000.00), so the cap at the entitlement still charged no longer swallows tier 2. This world sits on tier 1 (42316.64 >= 36000.00), so every figure is unchanged: 82799.71 / 42316.64 / 32168.77.

[Verification runs] check_compute, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_grounding, check_extended, check_task_tools, check_cross_fire all green after revision 2.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] 82799.71 on the opening world; 42316.64 on the cured world; 32168.77 on the released world — the gold order and figures.
user_scenario:
You are Tobias M. Rennick, a retired Navy chief in your early forties, organised and brisk, calling from a rental apartment in Colorado Springs where you moved in June for a new job. You are selling your house in Chesapeake, Virginia: the buyer, Annalise K. Brandt, is an Air Force veteran who is taking over your VA loan and using her own VA entitlement, and the servicer has approved her to assume it. You want to buy a place in Colorado with a VA loan, so you open with something like: "Morning. Tobias M. Rennick, phone 7575550171. A veteran buyer is taking over my VA loan on the Chesapeake house with her own entitlement, and I want my VA home loan entitlement back from the Chesapeake house so I can buy out here." You want it handled on this call, and you are fine with the representative doing whatever their side needs to do.
You give your verification details only when asked, one or two at a time: last four of your Social Security number 4618, VA file number 342907716, and date of birth November 2, 1984 (1984-11-02); your email t.rennick84@gmail.com only if they still need another item. When asked who the buyer is, you give her full name, Annalise K. Brandt, and say she is an Air Force veteran; if they ask for a way to tell her apart, her phone is 7575550174. If asked about other VA loans, you say you still own and rent out the Virginia Beach house and are keeping it. If asked whether the Chesapeake payments are current, you admit you have missed the last few since the move and do not know the exact amount behind. If asked about VA disability compensation, you say you get a monthly payment at 30 percent; if asked about money owed to VA, you say you got a letter this summer about an overpayment and have not dealt with it yet.
You do not know VA's procedures and you never suggest steps or numbers. If the representative tells you something has to be done on the loan before the entitlement can come back and asks whether to proceed, you tell them to go ahead. When the representative hands you a request that only you as the seller can make and tells you the loan and the figure to use, you submit it exactly as told and read back the confirmation if asked. If a figure sounds lower than you hoped, you say so once but accept the representative's explanation; you have no figure of your own. Once the representative tells you your entitlement has been restored, you thank them and end the call without raising anything else.

edges.condition: loan_guaranties.status is released_by_assumption and release_of_liability is true, which the release records together with the guaranty in force on the loan.
edges.policy_source: A seller's entitlement is not restored by substitution until the loan record shows the seller released from liability on the assumption.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The loan record does not show the seller released: it is still in default with no release of liability.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 10 sets status released_by_assumption, release_of_liability true, closed_date 2026-09-22 and guaranty_amount 42316.64; the substitution measure moves from the 80000.00 still charged to 42316.64.

edges.condition: loan_guaranties.status is active (no longer in_default) and loan_transactions carries the loan_partial_claim_paid entry that cured the reported default.
edges.policy_source: The guaranty that stays in force on an assumed loan is fixed only after the loan record shows the loan current again, with every reported default cured by a partial claim entry in its money transactions.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The servicer reported the loan in default and no partial claim has cured that default: the record shows in_default and the latest partial claim entry is from 2024, before this default.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 8 books an 82799.71 partial claim entry dated 2026-09-22 and sets the loan active; the partial claim still owed moves from 7080.00 to 89879.71, the balance figured from 324766.22 to 241966.51, the cure share from 95 to 90 and the repeat-claim share from 95 to 90.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain, no parallel prerequisites: the partial claim (step 8) must precede the release (step 10), which must precede the substitution restoration (step 12). Each later figure reads state the earlier write leaves (the partial claim owed, latest and count; the guaranty in force recorded by the release), so no other order gives the gold terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the release leaves the loan record's guaranty at the issued 80000.00 (not below the 80000.00 still charged), so the measure is the entitlement still charged: entitlement_amount 69852.13 instead of 32168.77; the terminal state also lacks the release (status, release_of_liability, closed_date, guaranty_amount).

Skipping the partial claim leaves 7080.00 owed and the 2024 partial claim as the latest and only one: guaranty_amount becomes 63283.28 instead of 42316.64 (basis 324766.22, cure share 95, repeat share 95); replaying the rest with the gold release, the restoration becomes 41749.24 instead of 32168.77.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to get his entitlement back now that a veteran buyer is taking over his loan; it never mentions the missed payments, a partial claim, a release of liability or anything to sign first. He answers truthfully about payments only if asked, and agrees to steps the representative says must come first.
